drivingQuestion: How can the coin be returned after twelve months given the time limits for cities and villages?
outcomeNote: The difficulty is answered in the next unit (Rav Ḥisda).

segments.he: וְאִם הָיָה מַכִּירָהּ אֲפִילּוּ לְאַחַר שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ כּוּ׳. הֵיכָא? אִי בִּכְרַכִּין, הָא אָמְרַתְּ עַד שֶׁיַּרְאֶה לַשּׁוּלְחָנִי. אִי בִּכְפָרִים, הָא אָמְרַתְּ עַד עַרְבֵי שַׁבָּתוֹת!
segments.en: The mishna teaches: «And» although these are the limits of how much a coin must be eroded in order for there to be exploitation, «if» the one who gave the coin to the aggrieved party «recognized it, he must accept it» back «from him even after twelve months» have passed, no matter how little the erosion affected its value; and he has only a grievance against him. The Gemara asks: «Where» did this occur? «If» it was «in the cities, didn’t you say» that he has only «until a period» of time has passed «that» would allow him to «show» it «to a money changer? If» it was «in the villages, didn’t you say» that he has «until Shabbat eves?»

moves.about: mishna lemma: if he recognised the coin he accepts it even after twelve months

moves.summary: neither in cities nor villages could twelve months fit
moves.about: twelve months contradicts the mishna's own limits for both cities and villages
